description: JSON canonicalisation (JCS, RFC 8785) as the signatures use it. Parse inputJson, canonicalise, compare with expected.canonical byte for byte; expected.error means canonicalisation must fail.

cases.name: keys sort by utf-16 code units
cases.description: Sorting is by UTF-16 code units, not code points: U+1F600 (surrogates D83D DE00) sorts before U+FB01, and capitals before lowercase.

cases.name: numbers
cases.description: Numbers print in their shortest ECMAScript form. 9007199254740993 is past double precision and parses as 9007199254740992 (I-JSON keeps integers within 2^53).

cases.name: string escapes
cases.description: Only the quote, the backslash and control characters are escaped; \b \f \n \r \t use their short forms, other controls below U+0020 \u00xx in lowercase. The slash and U+007F stay literal.

cases.name: unicode stays literal
cases.description: Non-ASCII characters, U+2028 and U+2029 are written as themselves, not escaped.

cases.name: markup stays literal
cases.description: JCS leaves < > & alone. Only a step block escapes them (see blocks.json), after canonicalisation.

cases.name: nesting at the limit
cases.description: 65 nested arrays, 64 levels below the top: the deepest this implementation canonicalises (protocol 4.2 caps a step at 64 levels).

cases.name: non-finite number
cases.description: 1e400 parses to infinity, which JSON cannot hold: refused.
